findings.evidence: "This workspace holds 4 projects" followed by a `<ul>` listing only 3 items (Holiday Campaign Assets, Support Backlog Triage, Mobile App Revamp)
findings.fix: Either add the missing 4th project to the list, correct the stated count to 3, or add a visible label like "Recently viewed" to clarify the list is only a subset.
findings.location: workspace-overview section, intro paragraph and project list
findings.violation: The stated project count doesn't match the number of items shown, and nothing labels the list as a subset (e.g., "recent"), so a reader can't tell whether the count or the list is wrong.

findings.fix: Rename the id to "workspace-overview-settings-link" to match the link's text and destination.
findings.violation: The id implies the link relates generically to "projects," but the link text and destination are about project *settings*, so the id doesn't match its own control.

findings.evidence: `<button id="project-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` inside a `<form>` with no action attribute and no linked confirmation section
findings.fix: Add a confirmation state (or visible success message) that Save transitions to, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the mockup.
findings.violation: Clicking Save has no defined destination or confirmation state, unlike the Invite and Archive flows in the same document, which transition to explicit confirmation screens.

findings.fix: Add visible text (e.g., "Duplicate") or an icon inside the button, keeping the aria-label as a supplement.
findings.violation: The button has no visible text or icon content, so sighted users see an empty, unlabeled control even though it has an aria-label for assistive tech.

findings.evidence: `<button id="project-settings-duplicate-btn" ...></button>` has no associated target section
findings.fix: Add a duplicate-confirm (or duplicate-result) section and link the button to it, mirroring the archive flow.
findings.violation: Unlike "Archive project," which leads to an archive-confirm section, "Duplicate project" has no corresponding confirmation or result page, making it a dead end in the mockup.

findings.fix: Change this control to a `<button>` instead of an `<a>`.
findings.violation: A destructive, state-changing action is implemented as an anchor link rather than a button, which is semantically incorrect since links imply navigation, not performing an action.

findings.evidence: `` and separately `Continue`
findings.fix: Remove the redundant Save button or give it a distinct, clarified purpose (e.g., "Save as draft"), leaving one clear control that sends the invite.
findings.violation: Two controls appear to both finalize the invite (an undefined Save submit, and a Continue link that actually navigates to "invite sent"), making it unclear what Save does or how it differs from Continue.

findings.evidence: "An invite was sent to the address entered above."
findings.fix: Reword to "An invite was sent to the email address you entered" without relying on spatial position.
findings.violation: "above" refers to the email input on the previous, now separate, screen, which no longer appears above this confirmation message, making the reference disorienting.

findings.evidence: "You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list."
findings.fix: Add an archived-projects-list section reachable from project-archived/workspace-overview, or remove the claim if out of scope.
findings.violation: No "archived projects list" page or link exists anywhere in the document, so this references a feature that isn't actually part of the mockup.

findings.evidence: `<button id="notification-settings-save-btn" type="submit">Save</button>` inside a `<form>` with no action attribute and no linked confirmation section
findings.fix: Add a confirmation message or state transition after Save, consistent with other completed actions in the mockup.
